record_identity.title: At least 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis stopped in live Wuhan traffic during a system failure

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 31 March 2026 Apollo Go Wuhan fleet outage
incident_identity.date_basis: Wuhan traffic police reported that calls began at approximately 20:57 on 31 March 2026; Reuters and AIID record the same occurrence.

summary: A reported system failure caused at least 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis in Wuhan to stop in live traffic, including on elevated roads, stranding passengers until police and company personnel responded. Authorities reported that passengers exited safely and no injuries were recorded. The technical root cause remains under investigation in the public record. Later reporting attributed a suspension of new robotaxi permits and Wuhan operations to authorities’ response.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters reports Wuhan traffic police described the event as a system failure affecting more than 100 Apollo Go vehicles. AIID Incident 1460 preserves the same occurrence and affected-system entities. Public evidence establishes correlated fleet-wide stoppage and passenger stranding but not the specific failing component. Reuters attributes the at-least-one-hundred count to a police officer. Doors could open, but traffic made some passengers hesitant to exit. Later licence and Wuhan-service suspension remains reported policy action; a formal decision and final root-cause finding were not retrieved.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates a material correlated-failure mode in embodied autonomous infrastructure: a shared system failure can simultaneously immobilise a large fleet in live road environments. Without a confirmed root cause, VIGIL does not infer whether the mechanism involved central control, communications, cloud infrastructure, fleet orchestration or vehicle-local software. Stopped vehicles and safe passenger exit do not establish the execution/continuation decisions needed for bounded safe-exit success. That role becomes ambiguous; control availability/state remain unresolved. The outage’s root cause and repair remain unknown. The robust-functioning assessment is Not aligned for the fleet stoppage. The fail-safe response assessment is Boundary because the response decisions and resulting safety-state evaluation are not available.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A shared failure can immobilise many autonomous vehicles at once, turning a component or fleet dependency into a city-scale operational disruption. Embodied systems therefore need continuity, fail-safe behaviour and correlated-dependency controls that are assessed at fleet level as well as vehicle level.
assessment_boundaries: The specific technical root cause and failing component are not established in the reviewed public evidence.
The evidence does not establish whether the vehicles departed from a particular designed fallback state because the relevant design requirement is not public.
